title: Aptis Writing Part 4
instruction: Viết email cho bạn 40-75 từ và email formal 120-225 từ
note: Giữ nguyên tuyệt đối thứ tự set và thứ tự câu hỏi theo HTML nguồn. Mỗi set giữ nguyên Club notice (title + body) ở cấp ngoài, sau đó là 2 email prompts. Một số prompt ghi riêng 'about 40-50 words', 'about 50 words' hoặc 'about 120-150 words'; thông tin này được giữ trong embedded_word_instruction, còn word_limit lấy nguyên từ textarea nguồn.

notice.title: Fashion Club – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Fashion Club is planning an event with famous designers who will discuss their work and answer members’ questions. Some members prefer an online meeting because it would be convenient and inexpensive, while others want a live fashion-show-style event. Please tell us which format you prefer, explain your reasons, and suggest how the event should be organised.

questions.prompt: Write to a friend to say which way of organizing the event you prefer. (about 40-50 words)
Write to the club manager to explain which option you prefer and why. (about 120-150 words)

notice.title: Social Club – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Social Club is planning an event to help people meet others and make new friends. We are considering two formats: an online event that is easy to join from home, or an in-person event with face-to-face activities. Please tell us which option you prefer, how you feel about the plan, and what activities should be included.

questions.prompt: Write an email to your friend about your feelings and opinions. (about 50 words)
Write an email to the manager about your feelings and opinions. (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Television Club – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Television Club is planning its first face-to-face international conference. Many members come from different countries and have only communicated online, so this will be an opportunity for everyone to meet in person. Please suggest a suitable venue and activities that could help members get to know one another, exchange ideas, and enjoy the event.

questions.prompt: Write to your friend. (about 50 words)
Write to the manager of the club. (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Book Club - Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
From next month, the Book Club will no longer be able to provide members with one free book each month. In addition, problems with our delivery service mean that orders may take four to six weeks to arrive. We apologise for these changes and would like to hear your reactions, suggestions for improving the service, and ideas for alternative member benefits.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words).
Write an email to the president of the club (about 120-150 words).

notice.title: Art Club – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Art Club is planning a public talk to attract more interest in our activities and encourage both younger and older people to join. We would like to invite a well-known artist, but we have not yet chosen the speaker or the topic. Please recommend a suitable artist, suggest an engaging subject, and explain how the event could appeal to different age groups.

questions.prompt: Write an email to your friend (about 50 words)
Write an email to the organizer/manager (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Language Club (V1) – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
You have been studying English at the American Dream Center for two months and have found the course effective, practical, and enjoyable. You would like to recommend it to a friend. However, you have also registered for the next course but can no longer attend because your personal schedule has changed. Please explain the situation and suggest a suitable solution.

questions.prompt: Write an email to your friend. Recommend the course. (about 50 words)
Write to the club manager: you registered but can’t attend; describe feelings, reasons, and what you would like to do. (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Technology Club – Part 4 (Version 1)
notice.body:
Dear members,
Our website is an important place for members to share ideas, but recently some comments have been rude or negative. The club is considering changing the website so that every comment shows the writer’s real identity. Please give your opinion on this proposal and suggest other ways to encourage respectful discussion while protecting members’ privacy.

questions.prompt: Write an email to your friend. (about 50 words)
Write an email to the manager of the club. (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Debate Club - Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Debate Club is preparing a campaign to attract new members. We want to explain how learning to debate and speak in public can be useful in education, work, and everyday life. Please identify two important benefits, give examples of how these skills help people, and suggest an activity that could introduce beginners to the club.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words).
Write an email to the president of the club (about 120-150 words).

notice.title: English Club (V3) - Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
We are sorry to announce that this week’s English Club talk show has been cancelled because the invited guests are unexpectedly unavailable. As we do not currently have a backup plan, there will be no regular meeting this week. Please tell us how you feel and suggest an alternative activity, replacement speaker, or online event that could be arranged instead.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words). Write about your feelings and what you would like to do.
Write an email to the president of the club (about 120-150 words). Write about your feelings suggest possible.

notice.title: Fitness Club – Part 4 (Version 1)

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words).

notice.title: English Club (V1) – Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,

Some people welcome these changes because they make language more creative and modern, while others believe that language should follow clear rules. We would like to hear your views and the reasons why this issue causes such strong reactions.

questions.prompt: Write a letter to your friend to express your views. (about 50 words)
Write a letter to the club manager to express your views and explain. (about 120–150 words)

notice.title: Museum Club - Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Museum Club is considering introducing an entrance fee for members when they visit the museum. Please give your opinion, suggest a reasonable pricing policy, and explain whether discounts or free-entry days should be offered.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words).

notice.title: Business Club - Part 4
notice.body:
Dear members,
The Business Club wants to support local people who are planning to start small businesses. We are considering two proposals: creating a call centre where people can ask questions and receive advice, or offering free business courses in partnership with nearby universities. Please tell us which option would be more useful, explain why, and suggest how it could operate successfully.

questions.prompt: Write a short email to your friend (about 50 words). Write a letter to a friend about your choice and the idea.
Write an email to the president of the club (about 120-150 words). Write a letter to the club manager about your choice and why.
